stem: Arjun lends Rs 10,000 to a friend at a simple interest rate of 10% per annum for 3 years. What is the total simple interest earned?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Uses t = 1 year instead of the stated 3 years: 10000 * 0.10 * 1 = 1,000.

explanation: Simple interest is SI = P * r * t = 10000 * 0.10 * 3 = 3,000. The full time period of 3 years must be used; compounding does not apply here.

explanation_sections.punchline: The word 'simple' settles the formula instantly: SI = P * r * t = 10000 * 0.10 * 3 = Rs 3,000. No exponents, no compounding.
explanation_sections.approach: Name the formula before touching any number: SI = P * r * t. Map the three givens: P = 10000, r = 10% = 0.10, t = 3 years. Multiply directly. The test is whether you used the full t; dropping one year or compounding the interest are the only ways to go wrong.
explanation_sections.lesson: Simple interest scales linearly with time. The formula has no exponent. If you see an exponent in your working, you have switched to compound interest by mistake.
explanation_sections.timing: About 45 seconds. A single three-way multiplication. Option (1) at Rs 3,310 is the compound-interest result for n = 3; eliminate it in three seconds the moment you confirm this is a simple-interest problem.
